transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because... well, since my in-laws moved into our house, I’ve just been so keyed up and completely worn down. It's bleeding into everything right now. I'm snapping at my wife constantly, which isn't like me. 

And work is really taking a hit. I'm an agent, and lately I've been avoiding calls that I would normally handle immediately. It actually got to the point where I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart the other day just because I couldn’t think straight. I realized I needed to come in and talk to someone before I completely derail my life.
You mentioned avoiding calls at work, is this something you've been doing for a while now?
No, not for a long time. It's really just been going on for about a month now. It started right when my in-laws moved into our home. Before that, I was completely on top of things.
Have you been avoiding social gatherings or events outside of work since your in-laws moved in?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't been going out much, but that's mostly because I'm just so exhausted by the time I get home. I wouldn't say I'm actively avoiding seeing friends or anything like that. I just don't have the energy for it right now.
Have you been feeling sad or hopeless since your in-laws moved in?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. It's not really a feeling of being down like that. I'm just incredibly stressed and on edge all the time. I don't feel like things are hopeless, just... really overwhelming right now with them in the house.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things that are coming up, like the future or your situation with your in-laws?

No, I don't really sit around worrying about the future or anything like that. I mean, I know they're living with us right now, and that's just the reality of it. It's more about dealing with the day-to-day stress of them being in my space, rather than, you know, being anxious about what's going to happen next week or next month.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or difficulty sleeping since your in-laws moved in?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My sleep is about the same as it usually is, and I don't really get headaches. It's just the stress of the situation, not really any physical stuff.
Have you been having any recurring thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

No, not really. I mean, I think about them being in the house because, well, they're in the house. But I don't have, like, thoughts stuck on a loop or anything like that. It's just the constant irritation of the reality right in front of me, not really something I'm obsessing over in my head.
Do you feel like you're repeating certain behaviors over and over again?

No, not at all. I'm not doing anything over and over again. I mean, I just... I go to work, I come home, and I try to deal with the house being so crowded. But I'm not picking up any weird habits or repeating things, if that's what you're asking.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy doing?

No, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I still like the things I usually enjoy doing. It's just... well, it's a lot harder to actually do them or relax when the house is so full and tense right now. But the interest itself is definitely still there.
Do you feel like you're able to experience a full range of emotions right now?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, I don't feel numb or blank or anything like that. I'm definitely feeling a lot of frustration right now with the house being so crowded, but... yeah, if something's funny, I still laugh. If something's sad, I feel sad. My emotions are all still there and working fine, they're just mostly focused on how stressed and annoyed I am lately.
Are you finding it difficult to concentrate or make decisions at work or at home due to the stress you're experiencing?

Yeah, it really is. I mean, at work... it's gotten to the point where I actually nearly lost a musician’s contract recently. My head just wasn't in it. My managing partner even pulled me aside and questioned whether I could still be trusted with major negotiations right now. That was hard to hear. And at home, it's not any better. The conflict there has gotten serious enough that my wife is the one who pushed for outside help. So, yes, the stress is definitely making it hard to focus and handle things the way I normally would.
Are you having trouble maintaining your relationship with your wife due to your current stress and irritability?

No, I wouldn't say that. Our marriage itself is fine. I mean... we're definitely arguing more than usual because the house is so full and everyone is on edge, which is why she wanted me to talk to someone. But I'm not having trouble maintaining the relationship with her. We're just both really stressed out by the living situation right now.
Are you feeling like you're struggling to fulfill your responsibilities at home, outside of your relationship with your wife?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm still handling my end of things around the house. The bills are paid, chores get done... I haven't dropped the ball on that kind of stuff. It's really just the tension with everyone being under one roof that's the issue, not the actual day-to-day responsibilities.
Has your stress affected your ability to perform at your best in either your personal or professional life?

Yeah, I think I touched on this a minute ago, but yes, absolutely. Professionally, I'm just not performing where I need to be. Like I said, I almost blew that musician’s contract, and having my managing partner actually question if I can still be trusted with major negotiations... that really showed me how much I'm slipping. And personally, the conflict at home has gotten serious enough that my wife had to push me to get this outside help. So, yeah, the stress is definitely impacting my ability to function at my best in both areas.
Do you feel like the stress you're experiencing is significantly interfering with your daily life?

Yeah, like I was just saying, it really is. I mean, almost losing that musician's contract and having my managing partner actually question if I can still handle major negotiations... that's a huge problem for me at work. It's my livelihood. And then at home, the conflict has just gotten serious enough that my wife is the one who pushed me to get this outside help. So, yes, it's definitely interfering with my life across the board.
Are you avoiding any specific situations or places because of your in-laws living with you?

No, I wouldn't say I'm avoiding anything specific. I mean, they're in my house, so it's pretty hard to avoid them entirely. I still go home, I still do what I need to do. It's just... tense when I'm there. But I'm not staying away from the house or hiding in my room or anything like that.
Are you feeling overwhelmed by your stress most of the time?

Yeah, I'd say so. It feels like this constant weight I'm carrying around. Between the pressure at work and the tension at home with my in-laws, it just feels like too much to handle most days. I don't really get a break from it.
Would you say that the stress you're feeling is causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah, absolutely. It's... it's a lot of distress. Like I said, it's affecting my work, it's causing real problems with my wife. It just feels like everything is falling apart right now, and I can't seem to fix it. So, yes, it's very distressing.
Do you think your stress would decrease if your in-laws were no longer living with you?

Yeah, I think it definitely would. But, I mean, they are still living with us right now. The whole arrangement hasn't ended yet. So all this stress and everything I'm dealing with... it's happening right now while the situation is still active. It's not like they moved out months ago and I'm just still hung up on it. They're still in my house every day. If that were to change and they actually moved out, then yes, I think a lot of this pressure would drop.
